pictures.scene: Gerard van Honthorst, King David Playing the Harp — the king close up with his face thrown back and his mouth open in song, his eyes turned up into the light, a spiked gold crown set over a striped cloth cap and a heavy ermine and gold brocade mantle fastened at his breast, one hand come up on the strings of the harp beside him, for the choirmaster with stringed instruments according to Sheminith
pictures.name: pd_honthorst_king_david_playing_the_harp

pictures.scene: Guercino, King David — the king sitting back in his chair in a rose robe and a gold mantle with an ermine collar, a small crown pinned to his white turban, his eyes dropped and his bearded face turned down in thought, the sceptre held loose in one hand and the other laid out on a stone tablet lettered glorious things are spoken of you, city of God, a Psalm of David, O LORD do not rebuke me in Your anger
pictures.name: pd_guercino_king_david

pictures.scene: George Inness, The Coming Storm — the whole sky gone heavy and black over the meadow with one torn gap of pale cloud left in it, the farmhouse roof and its thin line of chimney smoke lying low under the dark, the trees going silver as the wind turns their leaves, and one farmhand in a straw hat walking home over the field with his pitchfork on his shoulder, or discipline me in Your wrath, be merciful to me O LORD for I am frail
pictures.name: pd_inness_the_coming_storm

pictures.scene: Gabriel Metsu, The Sick Child — the child lying limp across her mother's lap in a yellow jacket and a white shift, her head fallen back on the woman's arm and her dull eyes turned straight out at us, the mother in a black cap and a blue skirt bending over her and holding her up, a little painting of the crucifixion hanging on the bare wall behind them, heal me O LORD for my bones are in agony, my soul is deeply distressed
pictures.name: pd_metsu_the_sick_child

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, Jeremiah Lamenting the Destruction of Jerusalem — the old prophet sitting alone against the rock with his head propped on his hand and his eyes closed, his white beard down over a fur-lined robe, the big book lying open at his elbow and the saved gold vessels heaped beside him, the burning city throwing its light up out of the dark behind his shoulder, how long O LORD how long, turn O LORD and deliver my soul
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_jeremiah_lamenting

pictures.scene: Eugene Delacroix, Christ on the Sea of Galilee — the little boat up on the green swell with its sail torn loose and flogging, the disciples hauling at the ropes and bracing themselves along the gunwale while the white water breaks past the bow, and Christ lying asleep in the bottom of the boat in a red robe with the gold light still round His head, save me because of Your loving devotion, for there is no mention of You in death
pictures.name: pd_delacroix_christ_on_the_sea_of_galilee

pictures.scene: Jacob van Ruisdael, The Jewish Cemetery — the white marble tombs standing out of the long grass under the ruined church with its empty windows and broken walls, a dead tree lying split across the whole front of the picture, the stream running past the stones, the storm cloud rolling over and one faint rainbow breaking through it at the left, who can praise You from Sheol, I am weary from groaning
pictures.name: pd_ruisdael_the_jewish_cemetery

pictures.scene: El Greco, The Tears of Saint Peter — the old apostle standing out in the half dark in a great yellow mantle over a blue robe, his grey head tipped back and his wet eyes turned straight up, his two hands gripped together in front of him, the ivy hanging down over the rock behind him and the heavy iron keys at his hip, all night I flood my bed with weeping and drench my couch with tears
pictures.name: pd_el_greco_tears_of_saint_peter

pictures.scene: Vincent van Gogh, Sorrowing Old Man — the old man sitting hunched on a low wooden chair by the fire in a worn blue working suit and heavy boots, both fists pressed up into his eyes and his bald head bowed right down over them, the bare boards and the plain wall shut around him, my eyes fail from grief, they grow dim because of all my foes
pictures.name: pd_van_gogh_sorrowing_old_man

pictures.scene: Ivan Kramskoi, Christ in the Wilderness — Christ sitting alone on a block of stone in the grey waste in a dark blue mantle over a red robe, barefoot on the broken rock, His hands locked hard together in His lap and His eyes fixed on the ground, the first cold light of morning along the whole empty horizon behind Him, depart from me all you workers of iniquity, for the LORD has heard my weeping
pictures.name: pd_kramskoi_christ_in_the_wilderness

pictures.scene: Maurycy Gottlieb, Jews Praying in the Synagogue on Yom Kippur — the whole synagogue crowded in under the stone arches, men in striped prayer shawls bent over the reading desk with their hands up to their faces and their eyes shut, one in a fur hat holding the dressed Torah scroll against him, a small boy looking out at us from the front and the women leaning over the gallery rail above, the LORD has heard my cry for mercy, the LORD accepts my prayer
pictures.name: pd_gottlieb_jews_praying_on_yom_kippur

pictures.scene: Albrecht Altdorfer, The Battle of Alexander at Issus — thousands of armored horsemen packed across the whole plain with their lances and banners standing up like a forest, one army breaking and streaming away toward the walled city and the tents, the mountains and the sea opening out beyond them and the sun going down in a burning sky over the whole thing, all my enemies will be ashamed and dismayed, they will turn back in sudden disgrace
pictures.name: pd_altdorfer_the_battle_of_alexander_at_issus

lines.text: For the choirmaster.
With stringed instruments, according to Sheminith.
A Psalm of David.
O LORD, do not rebuke me in Your anger
or discipline me in Your wrath.
Be merciful to me, O LORD, for I am frail;
heal me, O LORD, for my bones are in agony.
My soul is deeply distressed.
How long, O LORD, how long?
Turn, O LORD, and deliver my soul;
save me because of Your loving devotion.
For there is no mention of You in death;
who can praise You from Sheol?
I am weary from groaning;
all night I flood my bed with weeping
and drench my couch with tears.
My eyes fail from grief;
they grow dim because of all my foes.
Depart from me, all you workers of iniquity,
for the LORD has heard my weeping.
The LORD has heard my cry for mercy;
the LORD accepts my prayer.
All my enemies will be ashamed and dismayed;
they will turn back in sudden disgrace.
